strings.name: Simone Biles
strings.role: Artistic gymnast · Olympic and world champion
strings.summary: Biles advanced women’s artistic gymnastics through difficult skills and all-around strength, with several elements named after her. Across three Olympics, she earned 11 medals, including seven golds. Her public discussion of competition safety and mental health during the Tokyo Games also broadened debate about athletes’ rights.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026. The latest status comes from a September 2026 public interview. Olympic totals run through Paris 2024; no decision about competing in 2028 is assumed.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: 11 Olympic medals
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Through Paris 2024, earned seven golds, two silvers and two bronzes across three Olympic Games.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Six world all-around titles
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Won the women’s world all-around title in 2013, 2014, 2015, 2018, 2019 and 2023.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: Technical innovation
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: The FIG named the Biles II vault in 2023, bringing her total of named elements to five.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: 2028 participation undecided
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Told the Associated Press she was still considering the Los Angeles Games; this was neither a comeback nor a retirement announcement.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Laureus Sportswoman of the Year
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Received the award for a fourth time following her Paris Olympic performances.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Four medals in Paris
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Won team, all-around and vault golds, plus floor silver at these Olympics.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: World championship return
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Won team, all-around, beam and floor golds in Antwerp; a new vault was named after her.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Tokyo beam bronze
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Returned for the beam final after withdrawing from some events over safety and mental-health concerns, winning bronze.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Five golds at one worlds
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Won team, all-around, vault, beam and floor titles in Stuttgart.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Four golds in Rio
strings.timeline.event-07.text: At her Olympic debut, won team, all-around, vault and floor golds, plus beam bronze.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: First world all-around title
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Won all-around and floor titles in Antwerp, establishing herself at the top international level.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in the United States
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Columbus, Ohio; first encountered gymnastics at age six.
